title.en: Act IV: apparitions and the slaughter at Fife

hook.en: Macbeth goes back to the Witches and hears exactly what he wants to hear. Then he commits his cruellest crime: the murder of a family that has done him no harm.

objectives.en: Interpret the apparitions and their double meanings
Explain the significance of the murder of Macduff's family
Analyse the scene in England between Malcolm and Macduff

narration.en: Macbeth goes back to the Witches and hears exactly what he wants to hear. Then he commits his cruellest crime: the murder of a family that has done him no harm.

body.en: Macbeth demands answers from the Witches, who show him apparitions. An armed head warns him to beware Macduff. A bloody child says that no one born of a woman can harm him. A crowned child holding a tree says he will not be defeated until Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane hill. Macbeth feels safe, since these seem impossible. Then a show of eight kings, followed by Banquo, confirms that Banquo's line will rule. Each prophecy has a hidden double meaning that will trap him.

points.en: Bloody child: none born of woman can harm him
Crowned child with a tree: Birnam Wood to Dunsinane
Eight kings: Banquo's line will reign

title.en: On the board: Act IV in brief

body.en: Learning that Macduff has fled, Macbeth sends murderers to kill Lady Macduff, her son and their household: a senseless, purely cruel act, unlike the murder of Duncan, which at least had a purpose. In England, Malcolm tests Macduff by claiming to be lustful, greedy and unfit to rule; when Macduff despairs for Scotland, Malcolm knows he is honest. Ross brings news of the slaughter; Macduff's grief, and his insistence on feeling it as a man, contrasts with Macbeth's growing numbness. England supports Malcolm with an army.

points.en: The murder of Macduff's family: pure tyranny

title.en: Order the events of Act IV

steps.en: Macbeth visits the Witches at their cauldron
He sees the apparitions and the show of kings
He learns that Macduff has fled to England
Murderers kill Lady Macduff and her son
Malcolm tests Macduff with false confessions
Ross tells Macduff that his family has been killed
Macduff vows revenge and they prepare to march

explanation.en: Macbeth's false confidence leads to his cruellest crime, which unites his enemies.

problem.en: Why is the murder of Macduff's family a turning point for the audience?

steps.en: Duncan's murder had a motive (the crown); this has none except spite and fear.
The victims are innocent: a mother and a child.
Macbeth no longer hesitates or feels guilt beforehand: he has become a tyrant.
It gives Macduff a personal reason for revenge, setting up the final duel.

answer.en: It shows Macbeth's complete moral decline and gives Macduff his motive.
